content_summary: TRAI recommended that service licensees be permitted to use ANY of the surveyed network topology models (hybrid LPWAN+satellite, aggregator model, and direct-to-satellite); that all satellite types (GSO and non-GSO) be permitted; that any permitted satellite frequency band be usable; and that the EXISTING Unified Licence framework (in particular GMPCS authorisation) be suitably amended to cover such connectivity, rather than creating a wholly new licence.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Licensing Framework for Satellite-based connectivity for Low Bit Rate Applications

key_parameters.final: amend existing Unified License / GMPCS authorisation
key_parameters.name: licensing approach
key_parameters.proposed: new framework vs. amend existing (open question)

key_parameters.name: permitted models
key_parameters.proposed: asked which of hybrid/direct-to-satellite/other should be allowed

notes: Decisive date verified against TRAI recommendations listing (release date 26/08/2021) and PDF cover page dated 26th August 2021. A later item, 'TRAI's Response to DoT back reference dated 09.03.2022' (2022-05-05), is a follow-up reply to a DoT query and not a new decisive action.

content_summary: TRAI recommended that, in view of sufficient competition already existing in the cable TV distribution sector, there was no need to introduce any additional regulation or corrective measures on market dominance/competition (developments to be monitored instead). It separately recommended that Government facilitate voluntary sharing of last-mile cable infrastructure with telecom/broadband service providers.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Market Structure/Competition in cable TV services
notes: The recommendation explicitly declines new competition regulation ('no need to introduce any additional regulations or take any corrective measures'), a materially softer outcome than the regulatory intervention the consultation paper's Q2 raised as a possibility.

content_summary: TRAI recommended creation of a separate Satellite Earth Station Gateway (SESG) licence under Section 4 of the Indian Telegraph Act (not folded into the Unified Licence), at National service-area level, permitting SESG licensees to establish gateways for government-approved satellite systems and to provide satellite-based resources to any DoT/MIB licensee authorised to use satellite media.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Licensing framework for establishing and operating Satellite Earth Station Gateway (SESG)

key_parameters.final: separate SESG licence under Section 4 of Indian Telegraph Act, National service area, not part of Unified Licence
key_parameters.name: licence type
key_parameters.proposed: asked whether a specific licence is needed and what form

notes: Directly answers CP Q1/Q2 in the affirmative with a specific new standalone licence, one of the options the CP itself raised.

content_summary: TRAI recommended that all concerned Ministries/Departments adopt a unified, user-friendly digital single-window system covering licence/registration/permission issuance, renewal, modification, spectrum/numbering assignment, bank guarantees, M&A processing, show-cause notices and compliance reporting, using e-governance tools (Digi-Locker, digital signatures, analytics, automated tracking). This follows the ease-of-doing-business and reporting-simplification themes the consultation paper's questions raised.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Ease of Doing Business in Telecom and Broadcasting Sector
notes: Recommendations document is broad (multi-chapter, single-window system plus many sub-topics); content_direction assessed from its Chapter/Summary of Recommendations opening section (single-window system) rather than a full item-by-item comparison against all ~24 questions in the CP.

content_summary: TRAI recommended modifying PLI-scheme eligibility (global-revenue and cumulative-investment thresholds, separately for MSME/non-MSME, across product categories such as core network, access network, customer-premises and enterprise equipment) and recommended further PLI design features such as a local-value-addition criterion (minimum 50% component localisation, excluding certain semiconductor/PCB items).
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Promoting Networking and Telecom Equipment Manufacturing (NATEM) in India

key_parameters.final: revised global-revenue and cumulative-investment thresholds set per product category and MSME/non-MSME status
key_parameters.name: PLI eligibility thresholds
key_parameters.proposed: asked if current PLI eligibility criteria are effective

content_summary: TRAI recommended amending Model Building Bye-Laws and the National Building Code to mandate digital connectivity infrastructure (DCI) as an essential building component (alongside water/electricity/fire-safety), extending coverage to rural/semi-urban/remote areas via State Government bye-laws, bringing DCI provisions under builder-buyer agreements enforceable via RERA, and defining ecosystem roles for Property Managers and DCI Designers/Engineers/Evaluators -- matching the ecosystem-design question the consultation paper posed.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Rating of Buildings or Areas for Digital Connectivity
notes: A distinct, later consultation paper ('Regulation on Rating Framework for Digital Connectivity in Buildings or Areas', 2023-09-27, thread IN-TRAI-H-0019) led to a separate TRAI regulation in 2024; that is a different decisive action from this thread's 2023 recommendations.

content_summary: TRAI recommended assigning 5 MHz (paired) spectrum in the 700 MHz band to NCRTC, adjacent to spectrum already assigned to Indian Railways, and recommended that the same spectrum could also be assigned to other geographically-separated RRTS/Metro rail networks on a non-interference basis, subject to field trials for feasibility of sharing with telecom service providers.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Spectrum Requirements of National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) for Train Control System for RRTS Corridors

content_summary: TRAI recommended shortening the mandatory conversion/reconfiguration timeline for foreign M2M eUICC profiles on international roaming in India from the earlier 3 years to 6 months from activation of roaming (or on change of device ownership, whichever earlier); it also recommended that communication-profile switch-over be driven by the device OEM and specified which licence-holder categories may own/manage SM-SRs in India.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Usage of Embedded SIM for Machine-to-Machine (M2M) Communications

key_parameters.final: 6 months from roaming activation (or change of ownership)
key_parameters.name: eSIM roaming mandatory-conversion timeline

notes: Timeline was cut from 3 years to 6 months, a substantially stricter condition than the pre-existing rule the CP asked about reviewing.

content_summary: TRAI recommended that Government urgently adopt a cross-sectoral, risk-based AI regulatory framework, comprising an independent statutory authority (proposed to be named the 'Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority of India', AIDAI), a Multi-Stakeholder Body as an advisory arm, and categorisation of AI use cases by risk with binding obligations for high-risk uses.
decisive_document_title: Recommendations on Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in Telecommunication Sector

key_parameters.final: new statutory authority 'AIDAI' plus risk-based use-case categorisation
key_parameters.name: proposed regulator
key_parameters.proposed: asked what regulatory approach AI needs

notes: The consultation paper's questions were mostly definitional/exploratory (Q1-Q4 quoted); the eventual recommendation went further to propose a specific new statutory regulator, which the CP's own extracted questions did not explicitly float, so content_label_confidence is medium rather than high.

content_summary: No TRAI recommendations or regulation on this topic were found on TRAI's recommendations or regulations listings as of the censor date. A related Supplementary Consultation Paper (2023-08-03, thread IN-TRAI-H-0016) added further spectrum-auction-design questions on the same subject, but no decisive recommendations to DoT have since been released.
notes: Searched full TRAI recommendation listing (12 pages, 341 rows spanning 2000-2026) and regulation listing (11 pages, 330 rows) for 'aircraft', 'ground station', 'airport', 'ANSP' -- no matching decisive document found. label_confidence set to medium rather than high because TRAI's recommendation listing could in principle omit an item, though this is unlikely given the listings appear comprehensive and consistently structured.
